title: “Most Girls” by Pink
text: "Most Girls" is a song by American singer Pink, released as the second single from her debut album, Can't Take Me Home. It was released on June 6, 2000, and, after spending 16 weeks on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart, peaked at number four on November 25.

title: “Wifey” by Next
text: "Wifey" is a song by American R&B trio Next. The song was written by Eddie Berkeley, Keir Gist, band member Robert "RL" Huggar, and singer Lil' Mo for the group's second studio album, Welcome II Nextasy.

title: “Wonderful” by Everclear
text: "Wonderful" is a song by American rock band Everclear, released as the first single from their fourth studio album, Songs from an American Movie Vol. One: Learning How to Smile, on May 22, 2000.

title: “Oops!... I Did It Again” by Britney Spears
text: "Oops!... I Did It Again" is a pop song recorded by American singer Britney Spears from her second studio album of the same name.
listen: Oops!... I Did It Again Britney Spears

title: “I Wanna Love You Forever” by Jessica Simpson
text: "I Wanna Love You Forever" is the debut single of American recording artist Jessica Simpson. The song was released on August 30, 1999, by Columbia Records as the lead single from Simpson's debut studio album, Sweet Kisses.
listen: I Wanna Love You Forever Jessica Simpson

title: “Give Me Just One Night (Una Noche)” by 98 Degrees
text: "Give Me Just One Night" is a song by American boy band 98 Degrees, released as the first single from their third studio album, Revelation, on July 31, 2000. It was a success for the group, reaching number two on the US Billboard Hot 100 and on the Canadian RPM 100 Hit Tracks chart, becoming the band's highest-charting solo effort in both nations.

listen: Give Me Just One Night (Una Noche) 98 Degrees

title: “Take a Picture” by Filter
text: "Take a Picture" is a song by American rock band Filter. It was serviced to radio in September 1999 as the second single from their second studio album, Title of Record.

title: “Otherside” by Red Hot Chili Peppers
text: "Otherside" is a song by American rock band Red Hot Chili Peppers. It was released as the third single from their seventh studio album, Californication, and confronts the battles addicts have with their prior addictions.

title: “Big Pimpin'” by Jay-Z featuring UGK
text: "Big Pimpin'" is a song by American rapper Jay-Z. It was released in 2000 as the third and final single from his fourth studio album Vol. 3...

title: “Purest of Pain (A Puro Dolor)” by Son by Four
text: "A Puro Dolor" is a song recorded by Puerto Rican band Son by Four. It was written by Omar Alfanno and released as the first single of the second studio album of the band in 2000.
listen: Purest of Pain (A Puro Dolor) Son by Four

title: “He Can't Love U” by Jagged Edge
text: "He Can't Love U" is a song performed by American contemporary R&B group Jagged Edge, issued as the second single from their second studio album J.E. Heartbreak. Co-written by group members Brian and Brandon Casey, the song peaked at #15 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1999.
listen: He Can't Love U Jagged Edge

title: “Separated” by Avant
text: "Separated" is a song by American R&B singer Avant. It was written by Steve "Stone" Huff and Avant for his debut album My Thoughts, while production was helmed by Huff.

title: “I Wish” by Carl Thomas
text: "I Wish" is a song by American R&B singer Carl Thomas, released by Arista and Bad Boy Records on February 15, 2000 as the second single from his debut album Emotional. It was co-written by Thomas and Mike City, while production was handled by the latter.

title: “U Know What's Up” by Donell Jones
text: "U Know What's Up" is a song by American R&B singer Donell Jones. It was written by Edward "Eddie F." Ferrell, Darren Lighty, Clifton Lighty, Balewa Muhammad, Anthony Hamilton, and Veronica McKenzie for his second studio album, Where I Wanna Be, while production was helmed by Ferrell and Darren Lighty for Untouchables Entertainment.
listen: U Know What's Up Donell Jones

title: “Faded” by soulDecision featuring Thrust
text: "Faded" is a song by Canadian pop group soulDecision. Written by lead singer Trevor Guthrie and produced by Charles Fisher, soulDecision, and Femi Jiya, it was recorded for their debut studio album No One Does It Better.

title: “Only God Knows Why” by Kid Rock
text: "Only God Knows Why" is a song by American musician Kid Rock. It appears as the 11th track on his fourth studio album, Devil Without a Cause.
listen: Only God Knows Why Kid Rock

title: “Shake Ya Ass” by Mystikal
text: "Shake Ya Ass", also known by its clean title "Shake It Fast", is a song by American rapper Mystikal, released in 2000 as the first single from his fourth album, Let's Get Ready. Produced by the Neptunes, the song features a hook performed by Pharrell Williams, who is uncredited on various releases of the song.

title: “Bag Lady” by Erykah Badu
text: "Bag Lady" is a song recorded by American singer Erykah Badu for her second studio album Mama's Gun. Written by Badu and Isaac Hayes, the song is about a woman who is trying to begin a new relationship but has too much emotional baggage and can't get close to anyone.

title: “Meet Virginia” by Train
text: "Meet Virginia" is a song by American pop rock band Train, released as the lead single from their 1998 self-titled first album. Serviced to adult album alternative radio in March 1998 as Train's debut single, the song took over a year to gain popularity on mainstream radio, eventually reaching number 20 on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart in January 2000, becoming Train's first top-20 hit and their first single to a…

title: “Party Up (Up in Here)” by DMX
text: "Party Up" is a song by American rapper DMX, released as the second single from his third album ... And Then There Was X (1999) and was his most successful single (in the US).

title: “Case of the Ex (Whatcha Gonna Do)” by Mýa
text: "Case of the Ex" is a song performed by American singer Mýa. It was written and composed by Christopher "Tricky" Stewart (with his songwriting partners Traci Hale and Thabiso "Tab" Nkhereanyne) for Mýa's sophomore studio record, Fear of Flying (2000).

title: “Forgot About Dre” by Dr. Dre featuring Eminem
text: "Forgot About Dre" is a song by American rapper and producer Dr. Dre featuring American rapper Eminem.

title: “That's the Way” by Jo Dee Messina
text: "That's the Way" is a song by American country music artist Jo Dee Messina. The song was written by Annie Roboff and Holly Lamar, with Byron Gallimore and Tim McGraw producing the song.

title: “Swear It Again” by Westlife
text: "Swear It Again" is a song by Irish boy band Westlife. The ballad was released on 19 April 1999 in the United Kingdom as the first single from their self-titled debut album.

title: “The Next Episode” by Dr. Dre featuring Snoop Dogg
text: "The Next Episode" is a single by American rapper and producer Dr. Dre, released in 2000 as the third single from his second studio album, 2001.
listen: The Next Episode Dr. Dre featuring Snoop Dogg

title: “From the Bottom of My Broken Heart” by Britney Spears
text: "From the Bottom of My Broken Heart" is a song by American singer Britney Spears from her debut studio album, ...Baby One More Time. It was released on December 14, 1999, by Jive Records as the fifth and final single from the album.

title: “Crash and Burn” by Savage Garden
text: "Crash and Burn" is a song by Australian pop duo Savage Garden from their second album Affirmation. It was released as the album's fourth overall single, sent to radio in the United States on 13 March 2000; in that region, it was released as the third single.

title: “Yes!” by Chad Brock
text: "Yes!" is a song co-written and recorded by American country music artist Chad Brock. It was released in February 2000 as the second single and title from his album of the same name.

title: “The Best Day” by George Strait
text: "The Best Day" is a song written by Dean Dillon and Carson Chamberlain, and recorded by American country music singer George Strait. It was released in January 2000 as the first single from his compilation album Latest Greatest Straitest Hits.

title: Vicente Fox of the National Action Party (PAN) is elected President of Mexico, becoming the first president not from the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) since 1929.
text: General elections were held in Mexico on Sunday, 2 July 2000. Voters went to the polls to elect a new president to serve a single six-year term, replacing President Ernesto Zedillo Ponce de León, who was ineligible for re-election under the 1917 Constitution.

title: In southern Nigeria, a leaking petroleum pipeline explodes, killing about 250 villagers who were scavenging gasoline.
text: Gasoline or petrol (in other English-speaking countries) is a petrochemical product, a transparent, yellowish and flammable liquid normally used as a fuel for spark-ignited internal combustion engines (ICEs). It is chemically composed of organic compounds derived from the fractional distillation of petroleum and later chemically enhanced with gasoline additives.

title: July 11–25 – A summit meeting takes place at Camp David between United States president Bill Clinton, Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak and Palestinian Authority chairman Yasser Arafat, ending without an agreement.
text: The 2000 Camp David Summit was a summit meeting at Camp David between United States president Bill Clinton, Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak and Palestinian Authority chairman Yasser Arafat. The summit took place between 11 and 25 July 2000 and was an effort to end the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.

title: Air France Flight 4590, a Concorde aircraft, crashes into a hotel in Gonesse just after takeoff from Paris, killing all 109 aboard and 4 in the hotel.
text: Air France Flight 4590 was an international charter flight from Paris to New York. On 25 July 2000, a Concorde passenger jet operating the flight crashed shortly after takeoff, killing all 109 people on board and four on the ground.
